sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Critical Temperature (Tc)**: The temperature below which a material transitions from a normal conductor to a superconductor.
• **Meissner Effect**: The phenomenon where a superconductor expels all internal magnetic fields, becoming a perfect diamagnet.
• **Cooper Pairs**: Electrons forming pairs mediated by lattice vibrations (phonons) in BCS theory, allowing current flow without resistance.
• **Critical Magnetic Field (Hc)**: The external magnetic field strength at which superconductivity is destroyed.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Pure metals (e.g., Aluminum, Lead, Mercury). Low Tc.
Sudden loss of superconductivity at Hc.
Two critical fields (Hc1 and Hc2); allows magnetic flux penetration (Vortex state).
Prelims: Basis for high-field magnets and industrial applications.

items.definition: Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer theory explains conventional superconductivity via electron-phonon interaction.
Materials that superconduct above the boiling point of liquid nitrogen (77K), crucial for cost-effective cooling.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Medical Imaging**: MRI machines use superconducting magnets for high-resolution scans.
• **Transportation**: Maglev trains utilize Meissner effect for frictionless levitation.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Requirement of cryogenic cooling (liquid helium/nitrogen) and brittleness of ceramic materials.
• **Solutions**: Research into Room-Temperature Superconductors (RTS) to eliminate cooling costs.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'Type 1 is One-step, Type 2 is Two-step'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Type 1 loses superconductivity in one sudden step at Hc; Type 2 has two steps (Hc1 and Hc2) due to the vortex state.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Perfect Conductor' with 'Superconductor'. A perfect conductor has zero resistance but does not exhibit the Meissner effect.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Quantum Levitation' when discussing future transport infrastructure.

keyTakeaways: Type I are pure metals; Type II are complex alloys/ceramics.
Meissner effect is the hallmark of superconductivity, not just zero resistance.
HTS materials are the focus of current global research for energy-efficient power grids.
